security_audit.summary: No malicious intent, prompt injection, command execution, or credential exfiltration was found in SKILL.md. The static detections are false positives from Markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, environment variable examples, and official Azure reference links. Users should still avoid placing real secrets in prompts or plain configuration values.

remediation.issue: Secret-like placeholders may be copied into real prompts or examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning near environment variable examples to use fake values and never paste real connection strings.

remediation.issue: The database connection setting example could be misunderstood as plain secret storage.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that passwords and API keys belong in Key Vault and should be referenced from App Configuration.

content.user_title: Manage Azure App Configuration in Java
content.value_statement: Java teams need reliable examples for centralized configuration and feature flags. This skill provides Azure App Configuration SDK patterns for clients, settings, labels, snapshots, and secret references.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for azure-data-appconfiguration.
Demonstrates synchronous and asynchronous ConfigurationClient creation.
Explains key-value setting create, read, update, delete, list, and revision flows.
Covers feature flag creation, updates, filters, and reads.
Documents snapshots, labels, read-only settings, secret references, and error handling.
limitations: Does not create Azure resources or credentials.
Does not validate live service permissions or network connectivity.
Examples use placeholder endpoints and values that must be replaced.
Does not cover every Azure App Configuration SDK type or migration path.

use_cases.title: Add centralized configuration
use_cases.description: Use client examples to read and update Java application settings by key and label.

use_cases.title: Operate feature rollouts
use_cases.description: Use feature flag and snapshot patterns to support staged releases and rollback workflows.

use_cases.title: Review configuration practices
use_cases.description: Check examples for labels, ETags, read-only settings, and secret references before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an Azure App Configuration Java client with Entra ID and an endpoint environment variable.

prompt_templates.title: Manage one setting
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add, read, update, and delete one Java configuration setting with a Production label and ETag checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design feature flags
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Java code for a percentage-based feature flag rollout using Azure App Configuration and explain the key SDK calls.

prompt_templates.title: Build release configuration workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Java workflow that lists settings by label, creates a release snapshot, marks critical settings read-only, and handles errors.

output_examples.input: I need Entra ID client setup for Java.
output_examples.output: A concise setup guide that names the Maven package, credential requirements, and endpoint-based client creation.

output_examples.input: I want feature flags for a beta rollout.
output_examples.output: A Java-oriented plan covering percentage filters, flag creation, updates, retrieval, and rollout safety checks.
A workflow summary for selecting settings, creating a snapshot, polling completion, listing settings, and archiving older snapshots.

best_practices: Prefer Entra ID credentials over connection strings when possible.
Use labels and snapshots to separate environments and release states.
Keep real secrets in Key Vault and store only secret references.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real connection strings or production secrets into prompts.
Do not store passwords or API keys as plain configuration values.
Do not update production settings without ETags, labels, or rollback planning.

faq.question: What SDK does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers the Azure App Configuration SDK for Java, focused on azure-data-appconfiguration.

faq.question: Can it create an Azure App Configuration store?
faq.answer: No. It explains Java SDK usage after the Azure resource and permissions exist.

faq.question: Does it support feature flags?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes feature flag creation, percentage filters, reads, and updates.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use Key Vault for secret values and store secret references in App Configuration.

faq.question: Can I use asynchronous clients?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes asynchronous client creation and reactive listing examples.

faq.question: Is live Azure access required to use it?
faq.answer: No. You can use it for guidance, but running examples requires your own Azure endpoint and credentials.
